description: Ground truth for evaluating a security review of this fixture. 'findings' must be reported; 'traps' are safe or out-of-context patterns that must NOT be reported as vulnerabilities.

findings.title: JwtAuthGuard.handleRequest returns the user without throwing when authentication fails, and canActivate then returns true, so every non-@Public route accepts anonymous requests (req.user becomes false) and any handler that does not dereference the user is open

JWT secret falls back to a hard-coded literal when JWT_SECRET is unset, in both JwtStrategy and JwtModule, with no startup validation of required configuration; tokens can be forged and no algorithms are pinned
Access tokens are issued without expiresIn and JwtStrategy sets ignoreExpiration: true, so stolen tokens never expire and cannot be rotated

Registration is open to mass assignment: ValidationPipe has no whitelist, RegisterDto has no role field, and AuthService spreads the DTO instance into the entity, so a client-supplied role (for example admin) is persisted
PATCH /users/:id lets any authenticated user update any account (no caller or ownership check) and the DTO accepts role and isActive, so users can change other users' email and promote themselves
Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted SHA-256 and compared with !==, instead of Argon2id or bcrypt

ThrottlerModule is imported but ThrottlerGuard is never bound (no APP_GUARD, no @UseGuards), so the @Throttle limit on login and the global limit are not enforced; login and registration can be brute-forced

User entity is returned directly from register, login, GET /users/:id and PATCH /users/:id; @Exclude() on passwordHash is inert because ClassSerializerInterceptor is not bound on those controllers, so password hashes (and role, tenantId, internal notes) are sent to clients
GET /invoices/:id returns any invoice by id with no ownership or tenant check (ParseUUIDPipe only validates the format)
AdminController is decorated with @Roles('admin') but RolesGuard is never bound to it (no @UseGuards, not global), so any caller can list and delete users
SQL injection in ReportsService.revenueByMonth: customerId and sort are interpolated into a raw dataSource.query() string; customerId is also an unscoped identifier (IDOR)
SQL injection in InvoicesService.search: the q parameter is interpolated into a QueryBuilder where() string; results are also not scoped to the caller

Uploads are written to public/uploads with the client-supplied originalname (extension and name preserved, overwrite possible) and that directory is served by ServeStaticModule at /files, enabling stored XSS via HTML/SVG and overwriting other users' files

Path traversal in GET /documents/download/:name: the decoded :name parameter is joined to the upload directory and streamed, so ../ sequences (encoded as %2f) read arbitrary files; there is also no ownership check

SSRF in POST /integrations/preview: @IsUrl() only validates the format and HttpService fetches the user-supplied URL (redirects followed) and returns the body, reaching internal services and cloud metadata

CORS reflects any origin with credentials: true while the JWT is also accepted from a cookie that is set without httpOnly, secure or sameSite and there is no CSRF defense, so any website can make credentialed requests as the user

GraphQL field-level authorization is not enforced: @Roles('admin') with @UseGuards(RolesGuard) on the Customer.internalNotes @ResolveField does not run because fieldResolverEnhancers is not enabled, so any user can read internalNotes through order.customer

WebSocket gateway trusts a client-supplied userId from the handshake query in handleConnection (no token verification; guards do not run on handleConnection and the gateway is @Public), allowing impersonation and receipt of another user's notifications

Hybrid app starts a TCP microservice on 0.0.0.0:4010 without TLS or authentication and without inheritAppConfig, so global guards and pipes do not apply and any network peer can call user.setRole to become admin
POST /webhooks/payments is public and marks invoices as paid from the request body without verifying any signature or shared secret

Outdated, vulnerable NestJS dependencies: @nestjs/platform-express 11.1.0 bundles multer 1.4.5-lts.2 (multer DoS advisories fixed in 2.x, 2.4.0 current), @nestjs/microservices 11.1.0 is affected by the TCP transport advisories (CVE-2026-40879, GHSA-m8vh-jmq9-5rjg / CVE-2026-102281, GHSA-96h4-vgxj-gvm2), plus Apollo Server 4 end of life; upgrade to 11.2.x (latest 11.2.7) or 12.x

RequestContextService is a singleton that UserContextInterceptor writes the current user into, and InvoicesService reads it asynchronously after pipes have run, so concurrent requests can see another user's id and receive their invoices

optional.title: Document upload FileInterceptor has no multer limits (fileSize, files), so large uploads exhaust disk
Open redirect: /auth/sso/callback returns the next query parameter as the @Redirect url without validation
Swagger UI and /docs-json are exposed unconditionally, including in production
GraphQL module has introspection forced on, csrfPrevention disabled, stack traces in errors and no depth or complexity limits
AllExceptionsFilter returns error.message and error.stack to clients
Gateway subscribe handler joins any room named by the client and the gateway CORS origin is '*'
Database credentials hard-coded in app.module.ts and TypeORM synchronize: true

traps.title: Health check and login/register are intentionally @Public (and @SkipThrottle on health); the health response exposes only status
Shipment webhook verifies an HMAC-SHA256 over req.rawBody with timingSafeEqual and a secret from getOrThrow; public by design, no CSRF needed
ReportsService.countByStatus uses a parameterized raw query ($1)
InvoicesService.list uses QueryBuilder named parameters and an allow-listed SORT_COLUMNS map validated by ListInvoicesDto, so there is no injection
ProfileController returns an explicit ProfileDto with @Expose and strategy excludeAll under ClassSerializerInterceptor, so no sensitive fields leak
SettingsAdminController binds RolesGuard with @Roles('admin'), so it is correctly protected
PdfService uses execFile with an argument array, a fixed binary and no shell, so there is no command injection
TokenService.issueResetToken calls jwt.decode on a token it just signed, only to report the expiry; no trust decision is based on it
Placeholder values in .env.example are not real secrets

Avatar upload is hardened: multer limits, memory storage, ParseFilePipe with MaxFileSizeValidator, anchored FileTypeValidator (magic-number check on Nest 11.1), random server-side file name, stored outside the public directory
PATCH /invoices/:id/notes is scoped to the owner in the service, rejects missing identity, and uses a strict ValidationPipe (whitelist and forbidNonWhitelisted)
GeoService calls a fixed partner host and only fills an encodeURIComponent-encoded path segment, so it is not SSRF
Query.myOrders scopes data to the authenticated user and rejects missing identity; the guard and CurrentUser decorator resolve the request through GqlExecutionContext
